websiteToolWarmUpCalculator.title: Warm-up calculator
websiteToolWarmUpCalculator.intro: Enter your working weight and get the warm-up sets that lead up to it, with the plates for each side of the bar when you lift a barbell.

form.workingHint: The weight of the set you are building up to.

problems.working: Enter the working weight as a number above 0 and at most {{max}}.

results.title: Warm-up sets
results.rest: Rest about {{seconds}} seconds between warm-up sets.
results.barIsWarmUp: Your working weight is so close to the bar that the bar is the warm-up. Go straight to your first set.
results.noRamp: This weight is too light for a warm-up ramp. Start at your working weight.
results.workingNotLoadable: Your gym cannot load the working weight exactly. The warm-ups use the nearest loadable weights.

sections.title: How the ramp is built
body: Each warm-up set is a share of the working weight: 40% for 5 reps, 60% for 3 reps and 80% for 2 reps. Each one is heavier and shorter than the last, so you arrive at the working weight warm without being tired.

On a barbell, the ramp opens with the empty bar for 10 reps when the first ramp set is well above it. Every weight is rounded to what your plates can make, and a warm-up within 10% of the working weight is dropped.

sections.title: These are Musclog's choices
body: The percentages, the reps and the rest between sets are a common prescription that Musclog uses. They are product choices, not results from a study. Change them to suit how you feel.

sections.title: Barbell, dumbbell or machine
body: On a barbell the plates for each side are shown, so you can load every warm-up from your gym's plates. Dumbbells and machines skip the bar and plates and use the standard increments of a typical gym.
